title: Knock
description: A piezo feels a knock on the table: each knock toggles an LED and prints “Knock!”.

steps.clip: You need: an Arduino Uno and its USB cable, a breadboard, 1 × piezo buzzer, 1 × 1 MΩ resistor, 1 × 220 Ω resistor, 1 × LED, and some jumper wires.
Push the piezo in, its two legs in two different columns.
hints: Here the piezo is a sensor: a knock squeezes it and it makes a tiny voltage.
Its + leg is marked on top.
steps.goal: Put the piezo on the breadboard.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's GND pin → the blue − row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. The piezo's − leg → that same row.
hints: The − leg is the unmarked one.
steps.goal: Connect the piezo's − leg to GND.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the piezo's + leg to pin A0 on the Arduino.
hints: A0 is on the ANALOG IN side: a knock shows up as a jump in the reading.
steps.goal: Connect the piezo's + leg to A0.

steps.clip: Push the 1 MΩ resistor in: one leg in the piezo's + column, the other leg in an empty column.
hints: It slowly drains the piezo's charge so each knock is a fresh spike.
steps.goal: Put the 1 MΩ resistor next to the piezo's + leg.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the 1 MΩ resistor's other leg to the blue − row.
hints: Now it sits across the piezo.
steps.goal: Connect the 1 MΩ resistor to GND.

steps.clip: Push a 220 Ω resistor into the breadboard. Put its two legs in two different columns.
hints: A resistor works either way round.
It protects the LED — without it the LED can burn out.
steps.goal: Put the resistor for the LED on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one leg of the 220 Ω resistor to pin 13 on the Arduino.
hints: Put the wire in any hole in the same column as the leg.
Pin 13 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.

steps.clip: Put the LED in: the long leg in the same column as the 220 Ω resistor's other leg, the short leg in the next column.
hints: The long leg is + (the anode). Backwards, the LED stays dark.
Legs in the same column are connected — no wire needed.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's long leg (+) to the resistor.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the LED's short leg to the blue − row.
hints: GND is the minus side of the circuit.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's short leg (−) to GND.

steps.clip: Copy the code into the Arduino IDE and click Upload. Knock on the table next to the piezo: the LED switches and the Serial Monitor says Knock!
